prompt: A storage tank is being filled by a pipe at a rate of 15 liters per minute while a leak drains it at 4 liters per minute. If the tank currently holds 200 liters and its capacity is 500 liters, calculate how many minutes it will take to reach full capacity.
evaluation_criteria:
Net Rate Calculation: 0-5 (Evaluates correct net fill rate computation)
Time To Capacity: 0-5 (Evaluates correct division of remaining volume by net rate)
response_text:
To find the time it will take to fill the tank, first calculate the net filling rate by subtracting the leak rate from the filling rate.

Net filling rate = Filling rate - Leak rate
Net filling rate = 15 liters/minute - 4 liters/minute
Net filling rate = 11 liters/minute

Then, calculate the amount of water needed to fill the tank to its full capacity.
Capacity = 500 liters
Current amount = 200 liters
Amount needed = Capacity - Current amount
Amount needed = 500 liters - 200 liters
Amount needed = 300 liters

Now, divide the amount needed by the net filling rate to find the time it will take to fill the tank.

Time = Amount needed / Net filling rate
Time = 300 liters / 11 liters/minute
Time = 27.27 minutes

Therefore, it will take approximately 27.27 minutes to fill the tank to its full capacity.
